Credits and privacy

Object Lens is a small learning project for trying pretrained object detection in a photograph.

Your photos

The photo you select is processed in your browser. Object Lens does not upload that photo to a server. The browser still requests the website's files, including the model and the optional sample photo.

Labels, boxes and scores are model predictions. They can be incorrect, and a model score is not a measured accuracy percentage. Review the photograph when interpreting a result.

Object Lens

The project adapts the interaction demonstrated by Hugging Face's Transformers.js vanilla JavaScript object-detection example. The interface, input validation, background-worker integration, result handling, score filter and PNG export are project modifications.

Runtime and model

Transformers.js 2.17.2

Hugging Face's JavaScript library loads the pretrained object-detection pipeline used by this application.

Apache-2.0 license Versioned source

The browser bundle also includes Hugging Face Jinja 0.2.2. Its MIT license is included with these credits.

ONNX Runtime Web 1.14.0

Microsoft's runtime executes the prepared model on the CPU through WebAssembly. Copyright © Microsoft Corporation.

MIT license Upstream third-party notices Versioned source

The complete upstream third-party notice file is retained without modification.

The runtime bundle also includes these libraries: long 4.0.0 (Apache-2.0), flatbuffers 1.12.0 (Apache-2.0), onnx-proto 4.0.4 (MIT), protobufjs 6.11.3 (BSD-3-Clause) and guid-typescript 1.0.9 (ISC).

DETR ResNet-50

The detector was pretrained before this project used it. Object Lens uses Xenova's quantized ONNX conversion of facebook/detr-resnet-50, originally released by Facebook Research. This project does not train or update the detector.

The base model is published under Apache-2.0. The retained model cards identify the base model and the exact conversion used here.
